- Model consistently underestimates prices in early 2025, especially in March, suggesting a persistent downward bias.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 80+ to 85+), then correct sharply — model overreacts to recent highs.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: after a spike, forecasts drop too quickly, missing sustained momentum.
- In periods of falling prices, model fails to anticipate the full depth of decline — underestimates lows.
- Forecasts lag behind true outcomes by 1–3 days in early 2025, particularly in March, suggesting delayed reaction to market signals.
- Model overestimates volatility in low-price regimes (e.g., below 70) — forecasts too high, then collapse too fast.
- In March 2025, model systematically underestimates by 2–5% across all days — likely due to seasonal or policy-driven downward pressure.
- Model exhibits “memory decay” — fails to weight recent low prices heavily, leading to persistent overestimation of future values.
